summary: Surgical off-ramp for aggressive inference tuning causing sporadic hallucinations and tail latency
description:
Issue summary: Customer enabled a bundled inference tuning profile (async batching enabled, KV prefix prefetch enabled, quantization profile q4_0) during a feature rollout. Within ~2 hours they started seeing transient but repeatable issues: elevated 95p and 99p tail latency, a small but growing rate of 5xx streaming disconnects, and a set of correctness regressions (higher hallucination/repetition on a standard prompt set).

Impact: Affects ~5 nodes in BrightHealth's dedicated pool. Reported as production impact for several user-facing features (conversational summarization). Error rate ~3% (baseline ~0.2%), 95p latency increased from ~220ms to ~800ms for the affected tenant traffic. Customer is requesting a safe, low-risk off-ramp and verification checklist to restore baseline behavior while preserving telemetry for root cause analysis.

Environment details: Dedicated pool: dhp-nyc-2, tenant_id: th-bha-91, model pinned: rw-infer-13b-q4_0 (rolled from rw-infer-13b-q8_0), rollout method: staged-split 80/20 then 100%. Observed during peak US-East window.

Logs & telemetry references: See dashboard humdinger: https://grafana.internal.redwood/boards/d/tenant-th-bha-91/optimizer-health; traces: trace ids 9a3f7c2a..9a3f8b1c (sample streaming trace), slack thread #support-brighthealth (link: slack://channel/support-brighthealth/PLATFORM-4581), and recent commit for the tuning package: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/8fb2c3e (opt-pack: add q4_0 profile).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant config used: apply tuning profile 'aggressive-infer-pack' (async_batching=true, kv_prefetch=true, quant_profile=q4_0) via PATCH /v1/tenants/th-bha-91/config
2) Send representative production prompt set (see attached sample_prompts.json) at target QPS (production ramp to 20 rps / worker)
3) Observe 95p/99p latency in tracing and 5xx streaming disconnects in the API logs
4) Run the monthly eval prompt set for accuracy regression detection and compare token-level perplexity/delta
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: q4_0 quantization combined with aggressive async batching changes internal numeric stability causing token-level drift for some prompts (observed in eval diffs).
Observed increased scheduler queue depth on dedicated nodes correlating with 95p spikes — suggests batching interactions with kv-prefetch eviction/thrashing.
KV-prefix hits dropped by ~40% for affected tenant after enabling kv_prefetch (possible mismatch in cache key computation after quantization change).
No memory OOMs on the nodes; CPU (worker threads) and NVLink metrics show elevated utilization coincident with latency spikes.

Reproduced a reduced repro in staging by enabling the same profile and running the long-form summarization prompts; staging showed similar hallucination deltas but at lower magnitude (staging smaller workers).
mitigation_plan: Step 0 (safety snapshot): Create a tenant config snapshot: POST /v1/tenants/th-bha-91/config/snapshot -> snapshot_id=ss-20260312-01 (store snapshot id in ticket).

Step 1 (non-disruptive toggle): Disable KV prefix prefetch for tenant via PATCH /v1/tenants/th-bha-91/config { "kv_prefetch": false } and monitor 30 minutes for 95p latency and prefix hit-rate recovery.

Step 2 (conservative batching): If Step 1 insufficient, change async_batching policy to 'conservative' (reduce max_batch_size and batch_wait_ms) via PATCH and split 90/10 live traffic to the conservative config for 10 minutes.

Step 3 (quantization rollback): If latency or correctness not restored, revert quant profile to the last known-good (q8_0) by PATCH /v1/tenants/th-bha-91/config { "quant_profile": "q8_0" }. This is expected to be more impactful but restores numeric behavior.

Step 4 (worker drain/restart): If 5xxs persist after config rollbacks, perform a rolling restart of the affected serving nodes in the dedicated pool (coordinate with SRE; drain connections, restart agent).
Step 5 (traffic gating): If still degraded, gate tenant to lower concurrency (traffic-split to bypass dedicated pool to hosted) as emergency fallback and engage Eng for a post-mortem.
Owners: Support (Marco Diaz) to coordinate Steps 0-2; SRE (Lydia Chen) to execute Step 4; Eng (Ravi Kapoor) to own rollback to q8_0 if needed and validate model artifacts.
Note: All changes should be performed with monitoring alerts open (95p latency, 5xx rate, prefix-hit-rate, eval-accuracy). Keep snapshots and logs for post-incident analysis.
verification_steps: Run the monthly eval prompt set (eval-v1) before and after each step and record token-level similarity and hallucination metrics.
Confirm 95p latency returns to baseline within 30% of pre-change values for two consecutive 15-minute windows.
Confirm 5xx streaming error rate returns below 0.5% and no new unique error classes are introduced.
Validate prefix-hit-rate and scheduler queue depth metrics improved compared to the peak window.
Customer acceptance: Customer PKG engineer confirms conversational quality restored on a small representative subset (5 golden prompts).
resolution: Work in progress: Steps 0-1 applied. KV prefetch disabled at 2026-03-13T16:42Z; initial 30-minute monitor shows 95p latency dropped ~35% but token-level correctness regressions persist for a small subset. Proceeding to Step 2 (conservative batching) with 10% shadow traffic now.
